You are currently signed into the user’s Gumroad account and the product already exists.

- Product title: **NeuralShell Operator Tier**
- Gumroad page open: product editor

- Goal: build a strong, clean, credible Gumroad product page for NeuralShell

## Non-negotiables
- Do **not** publish immediately.
- Do **not** change account settings, payout settings, tax settings, email settings, or any unrelated products.
- Do **not** invent features that are not grounded in the project.
- Do **not** use hypey scammy language.
- Do **not** promise unsupported platforms or capabilities unless already clearly part of the project positioning.
- Save as draft when finished unless the user explicitly says to publish.

## What NeuralShell is
Use this positioning throughout the page:

**NeuralShell** is an offline-first, sovereign AI workstation / desktop shell concept centered on:
- local-first operation
- privacy-respecting design
- operator-style workflow
- structured workspace continuity
- model bridge / LLM control surface
- UI that feels like a serious command center rather than a toy chatbot

Use language that frames it as a serious operator environment, not a generic AI wrapper.

## What to produce inside Gumroad
Build the product page so it looks ready for a serious buyer to understand the offer.

### 1. Main product description
Write and paste a full Gumroad product description with this structure:

#### Headline
Use a strong clear opener such as:
**NeuralShell Operator Tier — an offline-first AI workstation for serious local operators**

#### Short hook paragraph
2–4 sentences explaining that NeuralShell is designed for users who want a more controlled, private, workstation-style AI environment with local model workflows, continuity, and command-center UX.

#### What this product is
Explain that this tier is for people who want access to the NeuralShell experience / package / operator-grade interface and related materials.
Keep it accurate and broad enough to fit the actual deliverables already prepared.

#### Core value bullets
Use bullets like these, rewritten cleanly:
- Offline-first, privacy-respecting workflow direction
- Operator-style interface and command-center UX
- Workspace continuity and session grounding
- Local-model oriented philosophy
- Structured product direction instead of generic chat UI
- Built for serious experimentation, control, and sovereignty

#### Who it is for
Include a section for:
- local AI users
- privacy-focused builders
- operator / power-user types
- people tired of shallow chatbot UX
- users who want a more grounded, workstation-like interface

#### Who it is not for
Include a short honesty section:
- not for people expecting a polished mass-market SaaS
- not for users who want everything cloud-hosted and hands-off
- not for people who do not care about local control, privacy, or operator workflow

#### What buyers receive
Write this carefully and avoid false specifics.
Use wording like:
- access to the NeuralShell Operator Tier package
- current included files / assets / interface materials provided with this tier
- future updates to this tier if the creator includes them
- documentation and operator-facing materials bundled with the release

If exact included files are visible elsewhere on the page, align with those. If not, keep this section generic and truthful.

#### Tone section
Add a concise paragraph that says the project is built around sovereignty, local control, disciplined UX, and a more serious relationship with AI tooling.

#### Closing CTA
End with a restrained call to action such as:
**If you want a more serious, local-first AI operator environment, this is the tier to start with.**

### 2. Product summary / subtitle / short description
If Gumroad shows a short description or summary field anywhere, fill it with something like:

**Offline-first AI workstation experience for privacy-focused operators who want more control than a normal chatbot UI.**

### 3. Receipt / buyer-facing clarity
If there is a buyer-visible receipt message or short post-purchase note available in the current flow, set it to something like:

**Thanks for getting NeuralShell Operator Tier. Your files and included materials are available in your Gumroad library. Check the included documentation first for setup, scope, and current release details.**

Keep it short and professional.

### 4. Cover / thumbnail / media
If there is already media attached, keep the strongest-looking one.
If no media is attached and the interface allows placeholder text only, leave media alone rather than inventing assets.
Do not upload random images.

### 5. Content blocks / page layout
Inside the content editor, make the layout readable.
Use:
- a strong opening
- short paragraphs
- section headers
- bullets where helpful
- no giant walls of text

### 6. Pricing or tier framing
If pricing is editable on the current screen and clearly visible, do **not** change it unless the user explicitly told you to.
If the price is not in view, leave it alone.

## Writing standards
- Clear
- technical but readable
- serious
- credible
- no cringe marketing language
- no exaggerated income promises
- no fake urgency
- no “revolutionary” fluff unless already present and grounded

## Suggested full description draft
Use this as the base text, then adapt to the exact fields available:

---

# NeuralShell Operator Tier

**An offline-first AI workstation experience for people who want control, continuity, and a more serious interface than a normal chatbot.**

NeuralShell Operator Tier is built for users who want a local-first, operator-style AI environment instead of a disposable chat box. The focus is on privacy-respecting workflow, a command-center feel, structured session continuity, and a more disciplined way to work with models and projects.

This is not positioned as a generic mass-market AI app. It is aimed at people who care about local control, a stronger workstation feel, and a more grounded interface for serious use.

## What makes NeuralShell different
- Offline-first direction
- Privacy-respecting workflow philosophy
- Operator-style UX instead of casual chatbot design
- Stronger session continuity and workspace grounding
- Built for local-model and serious-control minded users
- Designed to feel like a command surface, not a toy

## Who this is for
NeuralShell Operator Tier is for:
- local AI users
- privacy-focused builders
- power users and operators
- people experimenting with serious workstation-style AI interfaces
- users who want more control than a standard web chatbot gives them

## Who this is not for
This is probably not for you if:
- you only want a polished cloud SaaS with zero setup mindset
- you do not care about local control or privacy
- you want a casual consumer chatbot experience

## What you receive
With this tier, you get access to the NeuralShell Operator Tier materials and included deliverables associated with this release. That may include interface assets, packaged files, documentation, and release materials made available through this Gumroad product.

The exact contents of the tier should match the files and materials attached to the product at purchase time.

## Why this exists
Most AI products are built to feel easy, light, and disposable. NeuralShell is aimed in the opposite direction: more grounded, more controlled, more private, and more operator-focused.

If you want a more serious local-first AI operator environment, this is the tier to start with.

---

## Execution steps
1. Inspect the current product editor fields that are visible.
2. Fill the content area with the best adapted version of the draft above.
3. Add headers and bullet formatting so it reads cleanly on Gumroad.
4. Update any short summary / receipt text fields if available and relevant.
5. Review the full page for obvious formatting problems.
6. Click **Save changes**.
7. Stop and report back what was changed.
8. Do **not** click **Publish and continue** unless the user explicitly instructs you.

## Final response back to user
After saving, tell the user:
- what fields you edited
- whether the page is now in a solid draft state
- anything still missing, such as cover art, files, pricing review, or final publish review
